Unreal Introduction.exp: Introduction to Unreal and its ecosystem.

Hello Unreal:
Unreal Engine uses C++ and Blueprints for game logic. The primary gameplay class is AActor, which represents any object that can be placed in the world. The BeginPlay() method runs when the actor enters play, and Tick() runs every frame.

Create a C++ class inheriting from AActor, override BeginPlay(), and use UE_LOG to print to the Output Log. Compile and place your actor in the level to see the output.

Unreal Data.exp: Working with data and APIs in Unreal.

Actor Lifecycle: AActor is the base class for all gameplay objects in Unreal. Actors have a lifecycle: construction, BeginPlay, Tick, and EndPlay. Actors can contain components (USceneComponent, UStaticMeshComponent, etc.) for modular behavior. UPROPERTY() and UFUNCTION() macros expose members to Blueprints and the engine's reflection system.

Blueprint vs C++: Blueprints provide visual scripting for rapid iteration — ideal for designers and prototyping. C++ excels at performance-critical systems, engine extensions, and complex algorithms. Best practice: implement base classes in C++ with BlueprintNativeEvent functions, then let designers extend them in Blueprints. Use UPROPERTY(BlueprintReadWrite) and UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable/BlueprintImplementableEvent) to bridge both worlds.

Collision & Destruction: UE5's Chaos Physics replaces PhysX as the default physics engine. It supports destructible meshes via Voronoi fracturing, cloth simulation, and vehicle dynamics with modular suspension/engine/transmission. Use UPhysicsAsset for per-bone collision. Chaos handles large-scale destruction with breakable constraints and clustered particle systems.

Widgets & HUD: Unreal Motion Graphics (UMG) is the UI system for HUDs, menus, and in-game interfaces. Widget Blueprints combine a visual designer with event graphs. Key containers: Canvas Panel (absolute positioning), Horizontal/Vertical Box, Overlay, Grid Panel. Use BindWidget in C++ for type-safe access to widget elements. Widget animations create transitions without Tick(). Retainer Box caches widget rendering for performance.

Material Editor: Unreal's Material Editor is a node-based graph for creating shaders. Material Instances inherit from parent materials with parameter overrides — use them to create variants without recompiling. Material Functions encapsulate reusable node networks. Key nodes: TextureSample, Lerp, Multiply, Fresnel, Panner, Time. Use Material Parameter Collections for global material parameters accessible from Blueprints.

Large World Streaming: UE5's World Partition replaces level streaming for open worlds. One File Per Actor (OFPA) stores each actor in its own package. The world is divided into streaming cells loaded/unloaded based on player proximity. HLOD (Hierarchical Level of Detail) generates proxy meshes for distant objects. World Partition works with Landscape, foliage, and PCG-generated content.

Procedural Audio: MetaSounds is UE5's high-performance audio system using a node-based graph for real-time sound synthesis and processing. Build sounds from oscillators, envelopes, filters, delays, and convolution reverb. Parameters are controllable from Blueprints/C++ at audio rate. Replaces legacy Sound Cues with fully deterministic, CPU-efficient audio. Supports multi-channel output, sidechain compression, and dynamic music systems.

AnimBP & State Machines: Animation Blueprints control per-bone animation blending. The AnimGraph uses state machines, blend spaces, aim offsets, and layered blending per bone. Cached poses save performance by reusing evaluated poses. Sub-anim instances handle weapon/ability-specific animations. Root motion extraction drives character movement from animations. Use NativeUpdateAnimation() in C++ for efficient parameter updates.

Interactive World Objects: Smart Objects define interactive behaviors for world objects (sitting, leaning, opening). Combined with State Tree — a hierarchical behavior system with state transitions, conditions, and tasks. State Tree is lightweight, data-driven AI designed for smart interactions. Smart Object definitions include slots, interaction ranges, and behavior filters. State Tree replaces older behavior tree systems for character-scene interactions.

Procedural Content Generation: UE5's Procedural Content Generation framework uses a graph-based node system to generate content at runtime or in-editor. Nodes include terrain spawning, scattering, noise filtering, density mapping, and collision checks. PCG integrates with World Partition and Landscape for open-world generation. Custom C++ nodes extend the graph. Generate foliage, rocks, buildings, and entire biomes procedurally.

ECS & Crowd AI: UE5's Mass framework is a data-oriented ECS system for simulating thousands of AI agents efficiently. Fragments store data (position, velocity, AI state), Processors implement logic, and Archetypes define composition. Mass includes built-in LOD (full simulation → simplified → off-screen), crowd avoidance, movement, and sensory systems. Use Mass for crowds, wildlife, traffic, and ambient NPCs.

Input System: UE5's Enhanced Input System replaces legacy Action/Axis mappings. UInputAction defines actions with modifiers (dead zone, chorded, negate) and triggers (pressed, held, double-tap, tap, release). UInputMappingContext organizes context-sensitive bindings with priority layering. Use Player Mappable Keys for user rebinding. Supports gamepad, keyboard, mouse, and touch.

VFX System: Niagara is UE5's next-gen visual effects system. Emitters define particle behavior through Spawn, Update, and Render stages. Modules add forces, noise, collisions, and scaling. GPU particles handle massive counts (100K+) efficiently. Data Interfaces connect to external data (mesh, audio, AI). Use Niagara for fire, explosions, weather, magic spells, and environmental effects. System assets combine multiple emitters.

Terrain & Vegetation: UE5's Landscape tool sculpts vast terrains with heightmaps, layers, and erosion simulation. Use landscape brushes: sculpt, paint, smooth, and noise. Foliage system paints instanced vegetation (grass, trees, rocks) across landscapes. Procedural Foliage Spawner volumes auto-populate areas based on density, slope, and collision rules. Nanite supports millions of foliage instances with minimal overhead.

Sequencer & Cutscenes: Sequencer is UE's cinematic editor for in-game cutscenes and cinematics. Key components: Level Sequence (tracks actors, cameras, audio, events), Camera Cut Track (switches cameras), Take Recorder (record in-editor performances). Supports animation tracks, sub-sequences, and event tracks triggering Blueprints. Cinematic Camera actors with film presets and depth of field.

AI & Behavior Trees: Unreal's AI system centers on Behavior Trees — hierarchical task graphs with Sequence, Selector, Condition, Task, and Decorator nodes. Blackboard stores shared AI data (target, location, state). Environment Query System (EQS) finds tactical positions. AI Perception Component handles sight, hearing, and damage detection. Use AAIController to run behavior trees on pawns.

Legacy Audio & Attenuation: Alongside MetaSounds, UE supports Sound Cues (wave player, delay, mixer, modulator). USoundAttenuation sets distance falloff, reverb send, and occlusion. USoundConcurrency limits overlapping instances. UAudioVolume changes audio settings in world regions. Audio Mixing: master/submix buses, EQ, compression, and reverb effects on audio submixes.

Unreal Insights & Optimization: Unreal Insights is UE5's central profiling tool. Use console commands: stat fps, stat unit, stat game, stat rhi. ProfileGPU shows per-draw-call cost. Key optimizations: Nanite for high-poly meshes, Virtual Shadow Maps, Lumen scalability settings, HLOD merging, texture streaming pool, and PSO caching. Use -trace launch args for Unreal Insights capture.

Project Packaging: Package your UE project via File > Package Project. Target platforms: Windows, Mac, Linux, Android, iOS, and consoles (Xbox, PS5, Switch). Configure project settings: maps, default game mode, input, packaging (cook everything vs. by the book). Handle platform-specific SDKs (Steamworks, Epic Online Services). Create installer with NSIS or platform store submission packages.

Procedural Animation: Control Rig is UE5's procedural animation system that runs within the animation blueprint. Full-body IK using FABRIK solver, aim constraints, multi-priority IK, and spring dynamics. Control Rig graphs operate in the editor for rigging and at runtime for dynamic corrections. Sequencer integration for cinematic rigging. Python scripting for automation and batch rigging operations.

GAS Framework: The Gameplay Ability System (GAS) is a robust framework for abilities, buffs, cooldowns, and attributes. Core components: UAbilitySystemComponent (attach to characters), UGameplayAbility (skill definitions), UGameplayEffect (temporary/permanent stat changes), UAttributeSet (character stats). Uses FGameplayTag for blocking, stacking, and categorization. Widely used in AAA shooters and RPGs.
